subject: SOC 2: point-in-time snapshot definition and bridge letter request
messages:
From: Alex Sutton <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2: point-in-time snapshot definition and bridge letter request

Hi Marissa,

We're reviewing Redwood's SOC 2 Type II evidence for our procurement team. A couple clarifying items so we can close the control mapping:

1) For the period ending 2026-06-30, can you confirm how you define "point-in-time" coverage for host/service snapshots? Specifically: are snapshots considered inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC on the day (i.e., June 30 is included), or is the auditor's evidence taken at 00:00:00 and effectively excludes events occurring exactly at midnight?

2) Our compliance team flagged a short maintenance window that began at 00:00 UTC on 2026-06-30 for one service, and we'd like to know if you can provide a bridge letter explaining any gaps in log captures for that instant. We need something we can upload to our security portal by the end of this week.

If you can point us to the snapshot manifest or provide a short bridge letter, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Alex Sutton
Senior InfoSec Analyst | Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com

Quick notes while I pull details: our SOC 2 auditor obtains point-in-time artifacts (snapshot manifests, log rollups) from our evidence bucket. We typically treat the audit "day" as inclusive of the full UTC day, but I want to confirm the precise timestamp semantics for the services impacted.

- Definitive rule: are snapshot markers inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC on the day, or is evidence recorded at 00:00:00 with exclusion semantics?

Alex — I expect to get back to you within 24 hours with a definitive answer and an attachment if appropriate.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 02:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2: point-in-time snapshot definition and bridge letter request

Marissa / Karthik — technical summary below. TL;DR: evidence is inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC for primary snapshots; the ingestion outage at 00:00 UTC on 2026-06-30 affected only the realtime forwarder for the X-service and we have compensating artifacts.

- Snapshot cadence: nightly snapshot job runs at 23:59:59 UTC and writes a manifest to audit-bucket/snapshots/YYYYMMDD/manifest.csv. The auditor pulls from that manifest; we treat that as including the full preceding UTC day.
- Edge case: the realtime forwarder for X-service had a transient restart that began at 00:00:03 UTC on 2026-06-30 (a nondeterministic race with our autoscaler during a config rollout). That meant ~3 seconds of events were not forwarded into the BigQuery ingestion table at the exact 00:00 boundary for that service.
- Compensating evidence: we have (a) the snapshot_manifest_20260630.csv showing the manifest hash and snapshot time, (b) stream buffer logs that show the ingestion gap and recovered offsets, and (c) maintenance record with the change-id and PagerDuty incident.

I can produce:
- snapshot_manifest_20260630.csv (public auditor artifact)
- bridge_letter_2026-06-30.pdf (one-paragraph explanation signed by Compliance) referencing the incident and confirming no control degradation beyond the 3-second window and that replay buffers recovered all events.

Let me know if you want the raw buffer logs; I recommend we redact PII before sharing.

—Dev

dev_patel@redwood.com

Alex — thanks for the patience. Below is the confirmation and the artifacts we're providing for ACME-RFP-9982.

1) Snapshot inclusivity: Our auditor treats daily snapshots as inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC on the snapshot day. The nightly snapshot job runs at 23:59:59 UTC and the resulting manifest is the authoritative list of files the auditor uses for that day.

2) June 30 event & bridge letter: There was a short restart of the X-service forwarder that began at ~00:00:03 UTC on 2026-06-30 which impacted forwarding for ~3 seconds. Dev has attached the snapshot manifest and confirmed the replay buffers recovered the missing events. Per our standard process, we've prepared a short bridge letter describing the event and the compensating controls. Please find attached: 
- bridge_letter_2026-06-30.pdf (one-paragraph, signed)
- snapshot_manifest_20260630.csv (auditor manifest)

If you need the ingest buffer logs or a redacted incident ticket, we can provide those under the NDA — just confirm the recipient address.

Next steps for you: upload the bridge_letter_2026-06-30.pdf and snapshot_manifest_20260630.csv to your portal. If the procurement team needs a specific signer name on the bridge letter (CISO or Head of Compliance), let me know and we can update.
